statement: fd.weakform.StressEquilibrium is the mechanical equilibrium weak form for solids (3D or 2D plane stress / plane strain).
Geometric nonlinearities of StressEquilibrium are enabled through its nlgeom argument.
StressEquilibrium docstring: the weak form can be used for solids in 3D or with a 2D plane assumption (plane strain or plane stress).
StressEquilibrium docstring: it includes initial stress for nonlinear problems or if defined in the associated assembly.

StressEquilibrium docstring: it accepts geometrical nonlinearities if simcoon is installed (nlgeom in {True, 'UL', 'TL'}); in that case the initial displacement is considered and corotational formulations are selectable via the corate attribute.
StressEquilibrium docstring: for nearly incompressible materials a volumetric-locking avoidance method is selected via the incompressibility attribute.
StressEquilibrium docstring: the consistent geometric stiffness is enabled automatically for finite-strain tangent conversion and can be overridden with geometric_stiffness.

nlgeom parameter docstring: if True, geometric nonlinearities are activated using the updated Lagrangian method; the parameter is used only in the context of NonLinearProblems such as NonLinearStatic or NonLinearNewmark.
nlgeom parameter docstring: if nlgeom == 'UL' the updated Lagrangian method is used (same as True); if nlgeom == 'TL' the total Lagrangian method is used.
nlgeom parameter docstring: if nlgeom is not defined (None), the problem.nlgeom parameter is used instead.
self.nlgeom attribute docstring: set to False if geometric nonlinearities are ignored.
self.nlgeom attribute docstring: set to True or 'UL' to use the updated Lagrangian method (update the mesh).
self.nlgeom attribute docstring: set to 'TL' to use the total Lagrangian method (based on the initial mesh with initial displacement effect).

convert_tangent parameter docstring: convert the constitutive corotational Kirchhoff tangent to the formulation tangent (dS/dE for TL, spatial Lie for UL); set to False only when the constitutive law already returns that final formulation-dependent tangent.
WeakFormBase._initialize_nlgeom: if weakform.nlgeom is None it reads nlgeom from pb.nlgeom (problem-level fallback).
WeakFormBase._initialize_nlgeom: a boolean nlgeom=True maps to assembly._nlgeom='UL', and False maps to assembly._nlgeom=False.
WeakFormBase._initialize_nlgeom: a string nlgeom is upper-cased and accepted only if it is in {'UL','TL'}; otherwise it raises ValueError("nlgeom should be in {'TL', 'UL', True, False}").

StressEquilibrium.get_weak_equation: when assembly._nlgeom == 'TL' the strain is evaluated from DispGradient and initial_stress is read from PK2 (second Piola-Kirchhoff) with the initial displacement effect; otherwise (UL / linear) initial_stress is read from 'Stress' (Cauchy for the UL method).

okf concept file: nlgeom is only meaningful inside a nonlinear problem (fd.problem.NonLinear, fd.problem.NonLinearNewmark); it has no effect on a linear problem.

okf concepts/nonlinear-problem.md: in the verified 2D recipe the example sets nlgeom=True on the weak form while the problem keeps its default nlgeom=False; the explicit weak-form value is the one in effect.
okf concepts/nonlinear-problem.md: Geometric nonlinearity (nlgeom=True on the weak form) requires the external simcoon library.
okf concepts/nonlinear-problem.md: Elastic law + nlgeom=True is already a nonlinear (geometric-only) problem — no plasticity needed for fd.problem.NonLinear.
okf concepts/nonlinear-problem.md: EPICP (or ElastoPlasticity) adds material nonlinearity on top.
